BEFORE: Justice A.P.Bhangale, President
        Usha S. Thakare, Judicial Member


Per Hon'ble Smt.Usha S.Thakare, Judicial Member

Being aggrieved by common order dated 27/07/2011 passed in consumer complaint bearing nos.66/2008, 67/2008 and 68/2008, by Learned District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Mumbai Suburban, original opponent no.1/ appellant-M/s.New India Assurance Co.Ltd. has filed three independent appeals. By the impugned order, learned District Forum was pleased to allow consumer complaint bearing nos.66/2008, 67/2008 and 68/2008. Judgment and award is passed in favour of complainants by impugned order.

2

2. Consumer complaint bearing no.66/2008 is filed by Mr.Sambhaji B. Shinde and City Group Finance India Ltd. by alleging deficiency in service against the opponents. Complainant no.1-Mr.Sambhaji B. Shinde had purchased motor vehicle. Complainant no.2 - City Group Finance India Ltd. provided finance for purchase of motor vehicle. Motor vehicle was purchased for self earning and livelihood of complainant no.1. Said vehicle was insured with appellant/opponent no.1. Wife and son of complainant Sambhaji died in motor accident. Complainant no.1 was unable to drive the vehicle. It was difficult for him to make payment of loan/finance granted by the complainant no.2. Therefore, vehicle was given for plying to opponent no.2. Opponent no.2 was driving the vehicle as a driver. It was agreed by the opponent no.2 to repay installment of loan and on complete repayment of loan vehicle would be given in the possession of the opponent no.2. On satisfaction of loan amount, opponent no.2 will be the owner of the vehicle. The vehicle was in custody of opponent no.2. It was stolen during the intervening night of 9th and 10th September, 2005. Complainant Sambhaji filed report with police station on 11/09/2005. Claim was lodged with the Insurance Co. Surveyor was appointed by the appellant. However, claim was repudiated by letter dated 30/03/2007. Therefore, complainants have filed consumer complaint for claiming an amount of Rs.5,99,000/- with interest @ 18% p.a. from the date of claim along with sum of Rs.25,000/- towards costs of litigation.

3. Consumer complaint bearing no.67/2008 is filed by Mr.Naseer Ibrahim Hajwani and City Group Finance India Ltd. by alleging deficiency in service against the opponents. According to complainant no.1, he had purchased Tata Tempo vehicle for which the finance was provided by complainant no.2. Said vehicle was insured with opponent no.1/ appellant- M/s.New India Assurance Co.Ltd. Said vehicle was given to opponent no.2 for plying. Opponent no.2 was under obligation to repay loan amount. The 3 vehicle was in custody of opponent no.2. It was stolen during intervening night of 01/05/2006 and 02/05/2006. Complainant no.1 lodged police report on 02/05/2006. Complainant lodged claim under valid insurance policy. Insurance company appointed surveyor and sought report. However, opponent no.1/Insurance company repudiated the claim by letter dated 08/02/2007.

4. Consumer complaint bearing no.68/2008 is filed by Mr.Dhirubhai Prajapati and City Group Finance India Ltd. by alleging deficiency in service against the opponents. Complainant no.1 had purchased Tata Tempo vehicle for which the finance was provided by complainant no.2. Said vehicle was insured with opponent no.1/appellant-M/s.New India Assurance Co.Ltd. Due to personal difficulty, the vehicle was given to opponent no.2 for plying. Opponent no.2 had to repay the loan and after repayment of entire loan amount, opponent no.2 would be the owner of the vehicle. However, during intervening night of 26/02/2006 to 27/02/2006, the vehicle was stolen. Complainant no.1 lodged report in police station and on 03/03/2006, insurance claim was lodged with the opponent/appellant/ Insurance company. Surveyor was appointed and report was sought but the Insurance company repudiated the claim by its letter dated 30/03/2007.

5. Opponent no.1/M/s.New India Assurance Co.Ltd. resisted the claim by filing written version in each consumer complaint. It is admitted fact that vehicles of the complainants, namely, Mr.Sambhaji B. Shinde, Mr.Naseer Ibrahim Hajwani and Mr.Dhirubhai Prajapati, were insured with the Insurance company/appellant/opponent no.1. It is also admitted that motor vehicles were purchased by the complainants with the help of complainant no.2, who provided finance to them. Fact of theft of vehicles is not disputed.

6. It is admitted that all the three vehicles were insured with the appellant/ Insurance company and insurance policies were valid and in force on the 4 dates of theft of respective vehicles. It is submitted that insured vehicles were transferred to driver/opponent no.2. The insured vehicle was sold to opponent no.2 in each case. The agreements in respect of insurance of vehicles were between Insurance company and complainant no.1 in each complaint. But intimation of transfer of vehicles was not given to the Insurance company/appellant. On the dates of theft of vehicles, the concerned complainants did not have possession and ownership of vehicles with them. Hence, the complainants cannot ask for claims under the insurance policies. The claims of the complainants were rightly repudiated by the Insurance company. There is no deficiency in service on the part of Insurance company and consumer complaints are liable to be dismissed with costs.

7. All the three consumer complaints are based on common facts and common law point is involved. Therefore, learned District Forum proceeded to decide the consumer complaints by common judgment. Hence, all the above mentioned three appeals are decided by this common order.

8. In A/12/51 heard Mr.S.R.Singh-Advocate for Appellant and none present for respondent. In A/12/52 heard Mr.S.R.Singh-Advocate for Appellant and none present for respondent. In A/12/53 heard Mr.S.R.Singh-Advocate for Appellant and Advocate Mr.Digambar Thakare for the respondent Nos.1 and 3. Perused the documents on record and considered the admitted facts.

9. It is admitted fact that the vehicles of the complainants/ respondent no.1 were insured with the Insurance company/appellant. The vehicle of each complainant was stolen. Report about theft of vehicle was filed by the concerned complainant with police station. On the date of theft of respective vehicles, insurance policies were in force. Each complainant/ respondent no.1 lodged the claim with the Insurance company. Insurance company repudiated the claim of each complainant/respondent no.1 on the 5 ground that on the date of theft of vehicles in each complaint, the respective complainant did not have the possession and ownership of the vehicle. Therefore, they are not entitled for insurance claim.

10. It is vehemently urged by learned counsel Mr.S.R.Singh on behalf of the appellant that on the date of theft of respective vehicles, there was no relationship between the complainant and Insurance company/opponent no.1 as 'consumer' and 'service provider'. 'Insurable interest' would not get transferred only because of handing over of possession and use of vehicle and consent of insurer is required for transferring such insurable interest. Learned counsel Mr.Singh placed reliance on ruling of Hon'ble National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, New Delhi, in the matter of Sarfarjudden s/o.Sh.Yasin Khn v/s. Branch Manager, The New India Assurance Co.Ltd. and Mr.Ashok Kumar s/o.Sh. Yad Ram, in Revision Petition no.4444 of 2012 decided on 20/01/2015, in which it is held that "insured will not be entitled to compensation from insurer for damages to the transferred vehicle in the absence of specific contract covering risk for damage to the vehicle".

11. With due respect we submit that the ruling relied upon by the learned counsel is not applicable to the case in hand as the facts of the case cited supra and the case in hand are not the same. In the case cited supra, it is not in dispute that the vehicle in question had been sold to respondent no.2 - Mr.Ashok Kumar Yad Ram. It is not in dispute that the vehicle was stolen on 21/09/2005 for which FIR was lodged by respondent no.2 on 25/09/2005 and the intimation of theft was given to respondent/Insurance company by the petitioner. Respondent no.2 had applied to the RTO for transfer but on the date of theft, registration of the vehicle was in the name of the petitioner. Specific dates of application for transfer in the name of respondent no.2 as also the receipt of the request for transfer by RTO have not been provided by the petitioner. In the case in hand, registration of the 6 vehicle was in the name of complainant/respondent. Insurance policy was also in the name of complainant/respondent. It was never transferred in the name of original opponent no.2. Sale transaction was not complete. Complainant/respondent has control over the insured vehicle. Nothing is on record to show that complainant/respondent no.1 did not have ownership over the vehicle. In RTO record, registration certificate was in the name of complainant/ respondent. Opponent/respondent no.2 was never shown as registered owner of the insured vehicle in RTO record.

12. It appears that complainant had given his vehicle to opponent no.2 for plying. It is also observed that ownership of the vehicle was with complainant no.1. Learned District Forum rightly appreciated that in each case complainant no.1 had insurable interest.

13. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. v/s. Nitin Khandelwal in Civil Appeal no.3409 of 2008 decided on 8th May, 2008 in para 14 held as under:-

"In the instant case, the State Commission allowed the claim only on non-standard basis, which has been upheld by the National Commission. On consideration of the totality of the facts and circumstance in the case, the law seems to be well settled that in case of theft of vehicle, nature of use of the vehicle cannot be looked into and the Insurance Company cannot repudiate the claim on that basis."

14. Learned District Forum rightly appreciated the facts and circumstances of the case and arrived at proper conclusion. Learned District Forum rightly held that the Insurance company wrongly repudiated the claim of the complainants. Appellant/Insurance company failed to consider the report of the surveyor and wrongly repudiated the claim of the complainants. We find substance in the plea of the complainants/respondents that the 7 appellant/Insurance company is guilty of deficiency in service. Order passed by the Learned District Forum is just, legal and correct. It requires no interference. Consequently, all the appeals deserve to be dismissed. Hence the following order:-

ORDER Appeal nos.A/12/51, A/12/52 and A/12/53 stand dismissed. Common Order passed by the Learned District Forum stands confirmed. Parties to bear their own costs.
Pronounced on 7th August, 2017.
[Justice A.P.Bhangale] PRESIDENT [Usha S. Thakare] JUDICIAL MEMBER Ms 8
